**Finding: deviation (Section 13.2, ¶p0628).**

- **What the document does:** Section 13.1 sets a long multi-year term (through the Secondary Royalty Term). Section 13.2 gives Ono an at-will termination right, but only *commencing* on the later of the redacted anniversaries of First Commercial Sale of both the Binimetinib and Encorafenib Products, with a redacted notice period.
- **Why it fails the fallback:** Ono has no convenience exit during development, launch and the early commercial years — in substance no customer convenience right across most of a multi-year term, which the rule treats as walk-away. The notice period is redacted and cannot be verified against the 30-day preferred or 60–90-day fallback.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** at-will right available at any time during the Term, in whole or Product-by-Product/country-by-country, on thirty (30) days' notice, with refund of amounts prepaid for post-termination periods; 60–90 days offered as fallback in the comment.
- **Not flagged (in our favour):** Array has no termination-for-convenience right; its unilateral rights are limited to breach, insolvency and Ono's Competing Product activity. The Section 8.2 post-termination Competing Product restriction and Ono's Article XIV transition costs are noted only, to avoid double-flagging.
